implementation_notes: JDBC ships both halves of the pattern: java.sql.ResultSet is the connected form (a cursor bound to its statement and connection, forward-only by default), and javax.sql.rowset.CachedRowSet is the detached Record Set - disconnected while still implementing ResultSet, populated from a source ResultSet, serialisable (WebRowSet), with setPageSize paging and acceptChanges through a SyncProvider for write-back. What replaces a hand-written RecordSet class is this pair plus ResultSetMetaData for the column header. Use CachedRowSet (or a typed List<Row>) whenever the set must outlive the connection, and keep a plain ResultSet only for streaming consumption inside the transactional block.
pitfalls: A ResultSet dies with its statement/connection and is forward-only unless the type was requested at creation: returning one from a method that closes the connection hands callers a closed cursor - copy into CachedRowSet or a typed list first.
getLong/getInt return 0 for SQL NULL instead of null and coerce silently; wasNull() or getObject(Class) is needed to tell NULL from a real value.
CachedRowSet materialises every row and only writes back through a SyncProvider/acceptChanges; using it as if it were live produces lost updates.
